body: Multibaggers combine earnings growth with a rising multiple (Mayer, Phelps, Motilal). Start at a low multiple so both engines can work. Radico ≈ 7.5 × 5. NVIDIA post-2023 was earnings-only (multiple fell).
title: Twin engine: EPS growth × P/E rerating

body: Cases: Microsoft (Nadella 2014, $36 -> ~15x), AMD (Su 2014, ~$1.6 -> ~140x), Domino's (Doyle 2010, ~13x under him), Enphase (Kothandaraman 2017, ~400x then -90%), Meta (founder self-reset 2022-23, ~9x), Apple (Jobs 1997, then 2003-12 ~110x). Common pattern: (1) the stock is priced as a declining or dying business — P/E 9-15x or P/S <1x, often near-bankrupt; (2) the new leader publicly kills a sacred cow (Windows-first, low-margin segments, the old recipe, metaverse spending) and names a few measurable targets; (3) a single verifiable proof point appears early — Azure >100% growth, Zen benchmark demos, a +14% same-store-sales quarter, quarter-after-quarter gross-margin gains, an opex cut with a buyback; (4) returns come first from survival/rerating, then from EPS. Failure modes: Enphase shows a real operational turnaround can be overwhelmed by policy/cycle; turnaround investors should still ask whether demand is structural. Process rule for memory: don't buy the announcement; buy (or size up) after the first proof print, when the price usually still reflects the old narrative. Expected drawdowns even after the turn: -35% to -67% (MSFT 2022, AMD 2022).

data.signal: first measurable proof point after a public strategy reset

title: Turnarounds under a new CEO: the first proof print is the signal
